To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the importance of an attitude is positively related to the amount of counterattitudinal attitude change produced by a forced-compliance manipulation, but only to a certain point; the inverted U-shaped relationship between attitude change and attitude importance was found for both liberal and conservative subjects and for both high- and low-prejudice subjects.
the importance of an attitude affected the extent to which it was changed by the forced-compliance procedure, and that this relationship was curvilinear.

attitude change in the forced compliance situation is greater when the attitude is moderately than when it is extremely important to the person, and that the relationship between importance and change is curvilinear rather than linear.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship of the importance of attitudes to their changeability, as measured by the forced compliance technique.
the relationship between the issue importance of a counterattitudinally persuasive communication and attitude change.
the effect of issue-importance upon the attitude change that results from a forced-compliance procedure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the inverted-U relationship between attitude importance and attitude change is a function of the interaction between the amount of attitude change produced by the forced compliance and the amount of attitude extremity present at the time of the attitude change.

the inverted-U effect was due to the fact that moderate importance of the issues was associated with a greater amount of counterattitudinal argumentation than was the case for either low- or high-importance issues.
the forced compliance procedure is most likely to change attitudes when the attitudes are of moderate importance to the individual.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
forced compliance is a powerful attitude-change procedure which is effective for moderate importance issues and ineffective for both unimportant and highly important issues.
forced compliance procedures produce attitude change that is directly proportional to the importance of the issue.
the inverted U effect is a general finding that is not limited to any one type of dependent variable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inverted-U effect is a robust finding that is not due to variations of initial attitude extremity. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
the forced compliance procedure does not produce attitude change in a linear fashion.
the inverted-U effect is not due to variations of essay quality or initial attitude extremity.
